newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan risks China's wrath to downsize local govt.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan risks China's wrath to downsize local govt.

text.p: Taiwan said on Sunday it would soon start to reduce the size of its provincial-level government in a move sure to further provoke rival China, which has vowed to attack the island should it move towards independence.
"We will soon set up a special committee to make plans for the downsizing," said legislator Vincent Siew, head of the ruling Nationalist Party's constitutional amendment planning task force.

"We will invite the provincial government to send representatives to discuss the issue, and I believe it will do so," said Siew, who was seen as President Lee Teng-hui's hand-picked candidate for the next premiership.
But provincial government officials said governor James Soong had refused to be a rubber stamp and decided against taking part in what was seen a meeting of humiliation.
"Can you imagine the governor would talk with others on this. How humiliating it would be!" a provincial government source told Reuters by telephone.

The Nationalists and the pro-independence Democratic Progressive Party joined forces last week to approve a controversial proposal to phase out the provincial government during the National Assembly's constitutional amendment session.
Under the plan, the provincial system, which largely overlaps that of the central government, would be stripped of its autonomous status and become a nominal system.

The Nationalists say the move would save T$60 billion (US$2.2 billion) a year but analysts saw it as further fuelling Beijing's suspicions that Taiwan is moving towards full independence rather than eventual reunion with China.

The Republic of China, exiled on Taiwan since its 1949 loss of the mainland, has maintained a provincial authority distinct from the "national" government to bolster its increasingly untenable claim of being the legitimate ruler of "all China".

China, which views Taiwan as a renegade province subject to eventual reunion with the mainland, has warned that it will not tolerate any independence moves by the island and will use force if necessary to prevent such a push.
